subject: chemistry
question_text: Write the postulates of the kinetic molecular theory of gases.

verification.note: Chapter 4 (States of Matter) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.62-66), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The book prints NO Long Answer section for this chapter, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 2+2 mark split over the book's eight postulates is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

steps.label: The particles and their motion
lines: 1) A gas consists of a very large number of tiny
2) The molecules move randomly in all directions,
colliding with one another and with the walls of
the container, changing direction at each collision.
3) The actual volume of the molecules is
negligible compared with the volume of the gas.
4) The molecules exert no attractive or repulsive
forces on one another; they are electrically neutral.
steps.why: These four postulates build the model itself: what the gas is made of, how the particles move, and the two idealisations — point-size molecules and no intermolecular forces — that make the mathematics of an ideal gas possible.
common_mistakes: Writing the molecules are at rest between collisions. The motion is continuous and random.
Leaving out negligible VOLUME or no FORCES — these two are exactly what fails for real gases, so examiners look for them.
steps.memory_tip: Four model statements: many particles, random motion, no size, no forces.
steps.margin_note: Number the postulates. A numbered list is faster for the examiner to credit.

steps.label: Pressure, collisions and energy
lines: 5) The pressure of the gas is due to the
collisions of the molecules with the walls of
6) The molecular collisions are perfectly elastic —
no kinetic energy is lost in a collision.
7) The motion of the molecules is not affected

lines.text: 8) The average kinetic energy of the molecules is directly proportional to the absolute temperature: E ∝ T

steps.why: These four postulates connect the model to what is measured: wall collisions explain pressure, elastic collisions keep the energy constant in time, and the last postulate — energy proportional to absolute temperature — is the bridge that lets every gas law be deduced from the model.
common_mistakes: Writing elastic as molecules stick or slow down. Elastic means the total kinetic energy is unchanged.
Writing E ∝ T with T in Celsius. The proportionality holds for ABSOLUTE temperature only.
steps.memory_tip: Four outcomes: pressure from wall hits, elastic hits, no gravity effect, energy tracks absolute temperature.
steps.margin_note: E ∝ T is the postulate every gas-law deduction uses — box it.

insider_note: Eight numbered lines, two marks per group of four — completeness beats elaboration here, and E ∝ T written with absolute temperature is the line examiners underline.
